special_teams_analyst.prose: Washington's kicking is accurate short but shaky long. D. Stevens has been the only kicker all season, making 85.0% of field goals [kc1] over 20 tries [kc2]. From 50-plus yards the rate falls to 57.1% on 7 tries [kc3][kc4], so when CIN's offense forces a long try, treat it as close to a coin flip and push for field position first. Punting is the bigger lever: a 43.7-yard net average [kc5] on 40 punts [kc6], with 32.5% of punts landing inside the 20 [kc7]. Kickoffs go for touchbacks on 19.1% [kc8] of 47 attempts [kc9], and coverage allows 26.4 yards per return on 36 returns [kc10][kc11]. CIN returns average 26.0 yards on 43 returns [kc12][kc13], so there is no clear case to kick away from the returner; keep kickoffs deep and let field position decide. Special-teams EPA is near neutral for both: WAS 0.00 on 254 plays [kc14][kc15], CIN 0.01 on 236 plays [kc16][kc17].

report.title: CIN at WAS Week 11 Scouting Report
report.summary: Washington is near neutral overall but blitzes heavily and leans on the run on first down, so Cincinnati's protection and early-down runs will shape the game. Field position is the secondary lever, and Washington's kicking and punting give Cincinnati its clearest edge. Cincinnati's early-down run game and Washington's third-down passing tendencies round out the plan.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: Washington is close to neutral on pass rate over expected at -0.4 percentage points [oc1] over 553 plays [oc2], but its situations differ sharply. It throws on 57.9% of early-down plays [oc3] over 420 plays [oc4] but only 48.3% on first down [oc5] over 236 plays [oc6], so first down is the run-leaning look. On third-and-long it drops back on 92.2% of snaps [oc7] over 51 plays [oc8]. S.Diggs takes 21.0% of targets [oc9] over 281 targets [oc10]. The rush split is nearly even between J.Croskey-Merritt at 33.2% [oc12] and R.White at 32.2% [oc13]. Runs go right 42.8% of the time [oc15], left 31.8% [oc16], and middle 25.4% [oc17]. Rushing EPA is -0.1 [oc26], 21st in run EPA [oc28]. Red-zone drives end in touchdowns 59.1% of the time [oc30] over 22 drives [oc31], a small sample. Defend the right edge and keep early-down run calls from becoming predictable.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: Washington blitzes heavily: it sends five or more rushers on 42.4% of dropbacks [dc1] over 373 plays [dc2], the 3rd-highest rate in the league [dc3]. The blitz is not finishing drives, with a 4.8% sack rate [dc5], 28th in the league [dc6]. Cincinnati has allowed a 16.4% pressure proxy [dc9] over 365 dropbacks [dc10], so its protection is the main test against the blitz. Against the run, Washington allows a 45.6% success rate [dc12] over 206 run plays [dc13], while Cincinnati's run success is 41.4% [dc15], so the ground game is a credible early-down option. Red-zone defense is the soft spot: opponents score on 71.9% of red-zone drives [dc20] over 32 drives [dc21], a small sample. Cincinnati throws more on early downs than any team in the league, ranked 1st [dc24], so expect early-down passing that tests the blitz and the third-down defense.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Washington's kicker D. Stevens has made 85.0% of field goals [kc1] over 20 tries [kc2], but only 57.1% from 50-plus yards [kc3] on 7 tries [kc4], a small sample. Treat a long Washington try as close to a coin flip and push for field position first. Punting is the bigger lever, with a 43.7 yards [kc5] net average over 40 punts [kc6]. Kickoffs go for touchbacks on 19.1% [kc8] of 47 kickoffs [kc9], and CIN's return unit averages 26.0 yards [kc12] on 43 returns [kc13], so there is no strong case to kick away from the returner. Keep kickoffs deep and let field position decide.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Washington's TE Colson Yankoff is Out with a knee injury. He has a 14.0% snap share [ic3] over 8 games [ic4] and 1.8% of team targets [ic5] over 281 targets [ic6], so his absence is minor. Washington's C Lucas Patrick is Out with a concussion after playing 76.9% of snaps [ic8] over 7 games [ic9], so expect a backup center and possibly extra interior help against Cincinnati's pressure. Cincinnati's S Kyle Dugger is Out with a quad injury, on a 16.5% snap share [ic11] over 4 games [ic12], which thins its safety group. WR Andrei Iosivas is Doubtful with a thumb injury. CB Jalen Davis is Doubtful with a hamstring injury after playing 61.3% of snaps [ic19] over 3 games [ic20], and if he sits, Cincinnati's cornerback depth thins. G Brian Parker II is also Doubtful with a knee injury.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Pass protection against the blitz decides the first half. Washington sends five or more rushers on 42.4% of dropbacks [mc1] over 373 plays [mc2], and Cincinnati has allowed a 16.4% pressure proxy [mc5] over 365 dropbacks [mc6]. Keep a back or tight end in protection, use quick throws, and don't assume the blitz will finish plays. Early-down runs are the counter: Cincinnati succeeds on 41.4% of runs [mc7], against a 45.6% run success rate allowed by Washington [mc8] over 206 run plays [mc9]. Third-and-long favors Washington's passing, since it throws on 92.2% of third-and-long snaps [mc11] over 51 plays [mc12] and S.Diggs takes 21.0% of team targets [mc13] over 281 targets [mc14]. With Dugger out and Davis doubtful, win those downs with pressure and keep Diggs in front of the coverage. Field position is the last edge: Stevens is 57.1% from 50-plus yards [mc19] on 7 tries [mc20], and Washington's punt net average is 43.7 yards [mc21], so win the punting battle and make Washington attempt long field goals.
